svg.text: Carrier board: 30-pin USB-C ESP32 soldered onto a 14 x 20 hole perfboard, parts underneath
UNDERSIDE of the board, as you see it when you turn it over to solder: column A is on the left. Antenna end up, USB end down.
The ESP32 and the three connectors are on the other side (dashed). Everything else is on this side.
long leg N4, short leg N5
A hole is named by its column letter and its row counted from the USB end: K4 is column K, 4th row up.
The letters are printed on the top of your board. Dashed rings: the four M2 screws into the posts of the box.
Place the ESP32 by counting rows: VIN must be in K4. One row out and the USB socket misses its opening in the box.
solid line: bare wire or solder bridge along the holes
dashed curve: insulated wire, joined only at its ends
black dot: a component leg or wire end goes in this hole
black square: an ESP32 pin coming through from the top
On the top of the board
• ESP32 straight on the board, no socket strips: its two pin rows in
columns A and K, rows 4 to 18. VIN is in K4.
• MOTOR, PAW and LED connectors in column N.
C in E11, B in E10, E in E9
2N2222 / PN2222 / 2N3904 / S8050: flat face towards column N
BC337 / BC547: flat face towards column A
E12 to B12, stripe at B12
+ leg J4, – leg (stripe) J5, bent over to lie flat
towards column A. No wider than 6.3 mm
Three insulated wires, under the board
• Nothing under the board may hang lower than 7.5 mm. Push Q1 right down
or bend it over; the capacitor lies flat.
• The holes are plated, so each part can be soldered from the side it is
on. Cut its legs to 2 mm first so they do not poke out under the ESP32.
• Order: parts and wiring underneath, then the three connectors, then the
ESP32 last. Trim the ESP32 pins to 3 mm after soldering.
• Black (row 5) and red (row 4) run side by side: check there is no bridge.
• Check with a meter before powering it: no beep between VIN (K4)
